components.description: Condensed grotesk caps, tracked wide, set plainly on the paper. Reads as the printed heading on a form.
components.html: Most of what you pay for is re-reading.

narrative.overview:
The deck is an itemised bill for one week of work. Cream stock, black typewriter ink, one red stamp. Every slide is a line item on the same document: faint ledger ruling, dotted leaders running description across to amount, double rules under totals, and a perforated stub down the left margin.

The fiction was chosen for three reasons. It is LIGHT, which in a conference room where every other AI talk is a glowing dark keynote is the contrarian read. The talk already calls the product 'the receipt, not the subject', so the form is the argument rather than a costume over it. And an invoice settles the palette without debate: red is a charge, green is a credit, black is neutral. No decorative colour exists, because a bill does not have one.

It also makes the thesis arithmetic. The opening slide is not a claim about savings; it is four line items that sum to $61.13, and the room can check the subtraction.

Prior worlds: an Instrument Panel (light, blue, flat) was replaced by a Departure Board (matte black, split-flap cells, brushed steel, a flip cascade per slide). The board's mechanism was well-built and wrong — a headline that redraws itself on every advance competes with the presenter — and stripping it left the board too anonymous to survive. The Ledger replaces it outright, chosen over a brutalist type poster, an engineering blueprint, and a terminal.

rules.name: The Accounting Rule
rules.body: Red is a charge, green is a credit, black is neutral. A figure is red because it took money, never because it is important. If a number is neither a charge nor a credit, it is black. Emphasis comes from size and position, not tint.

rules.name: The Still Board Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a slide animates. Slides replace each other; their contents are simply there. The split-flap cascade was cut on purpose — do not reintroduce it or add a replacement. No fades, no counters ticking up, no reveals.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: The PAID stamp and its -5.5deg rotation appear once in the deck. Everything else on the page is typeset square.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere. Zero occurrences is the invariant. Paper does not cast light.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No neon, no blur, no gradient text. Depth comes from hairline rules, dotted leaders, and one-step paper changes.

rules.name: The Rows-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: Any comparison is a set of line items with shared columns and a right-aligned amount. A bordered box around body text is a card, and this world does not have cards.

rules.name: The Caps Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is uppercase, tracked wide, set plainly on the paper.

rules.name: The Container-Query Rule
rules.body: Type scales in cqw against the page's own inline size, never vw. The projector's aspect ratio is unknown.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Comparable figures are mono with tabular-nums, right-aligned in their column, so the subtraction can be checked from the back of the room.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears on the brandmark and focus rings. Two places. Never a status, never a fill.

antiPatterns: Glow, neon, gradient text, or blur — this is ink on paper
Body text in a bordered box (that is a card)
Colouring a figure for emphasis rather than for accounting meaning
A second total on the same page
Rotating anything other than the single PAID stamp; the retired -11 degree skew
Pure white paper — #F4F1E6 is the ground; white reads as a hole in the projection
Signal Blue outside the brandmark and focus ring
